paper.title_en: Flavomons in Matter Gradients: Ray Tracing and Amplitude Evolution
paper.abstract_en: Flavor instabilities develop in neutrino plasmas through the emission of flavomons, collective excitations of the flavor field. Matter gradients can sweep flavomons across the unstable wave-number range, halting their amplification. This effect is parametrically small for fast modes, where it was first identified, but we show that it strongly alters neutrino-mass-induced instabilities below the supernova shock, while leaving those outside largely unaffected. Dispersion relations alone, which are inevitably local, cannot determine the cumulative amplification of slow instabilities. Using the WKB approximation, we derive the covariant evolution equation for the flavomon amplitude along geometrical-optics rays, enabling a global treatment of instability growth and seeding.
